paragraphs: So he is listed in Yuchasin. The source is Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 4:2, which has R' Levi bar Chini. Hyman notes that he and chet interchange in the Jerusalem Talmud.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman explains the Hini/Chini spellings by interchange of the letters he and chet.

The checked paragraph in Jerusalem Talmud Terumot chapter 4 names Rabbi Levi bar China. Hyman supplies Terumot 4:2, Chini in the cited form and Hini in the heading. These ending and initial-letter forms and the literal locator are retained. His statement about he/chet interchange is an attributed observation, not a fresh corpus-wide finding; R’ preserves the title in his particular Chini form.
